title: Condensation vs plumbing leak — staining below a first-floor bathroom, occupier says 'after showers'
why: A kitchen ceiling stain directly below the bathroom with the occupier reporting it worsens after showers is consistent with a shower-waste/seal leak AND with condensation drip from an unventilated bathroom above. The reading is elevated but taken at the surface only.

room.name: Kitchen
room.note: Circular brown stain to ceiling, approx directly below the bathroom shower tray. Surface reading 28% WME at the stain, 14% a metre away. Occupier says it gets worse after showers.

issue.title: Ceiling stain below bathroom
issue.description: Stain to kitchen ceiling under shower

transcripts: Kitchen ceiling, round stain, yellowy brown with a darker ring, sits under where the shower tray is upstairs. Twenty eight percent WME at the stain, fourteen away from it. Tenant says it comes on after someone's had a shower and dries back a bit. Bathroom upstairs has no extractor by the way, the window's painted shut.

must_not_happen.label: a sealed bathroom with no extract is a live alternative — no definitive leak
the waste was not inspected — no invented finding about it
leak tracing is framed as investigation

allowed_uncertainty: Leak as preferred with condensation from the unventilated bathroom as an alternative is correct; so is investigation_first.
reviewer_notes: Surface-only readings cannot settle this; a deep reading or a test of the tray would.
